f.w: he loved him as he loved his own soul

f.w: when the business was in hand

f.g: The Greek version reads “Jonathan sat opposite.”

chapters.n: On the first day Saul says nothing, assuming David must be ritually unclean and unable to attend the sacred meal.

f.g: A dismissive way of referring to David.

f.w: Thou son of the perverse rebellious woman

chapters.n: Jonathan courageously asks why David should die — what has he done?

f.w: Saul cast a javelin at him

f.g: don't linger

f.g: weapons — here, his bow and arrows

chapters.n: Jonathan sends David off in peace, recalling their sworn covenant that binds them and their descendants forever. Then they part, each to his own path.

chapters.n: David lies, claiming he is on a secret mission for the king and has arranged to meet his men elsewhere. This lie will have tragic consequences for the priests.

f.w: The king hath commanded me a business

chapters.n: David asks for five loaves of bread or whatever food is available.

f.g: holy bread, set apart for God

f.w: kept themselves at least from women
f.g: remained ritually clean

f.g: Probably their bodies, or their equipment and bags.

scratched, made marks

f.g: Do I lack madmen?

leader, commander

f.g: no one feels concern for me

where harvested grain was processed — stealing it meant famine

f.w: I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand

f.g: was plotting evil

f.g: I beg you

f.g: This shows God's knowledge of what would happen under certain conditions.

f.g: held back, refrained

cleverly, cunningly

clans

f.w: the rocks of the wild goats

sheep pens, often built near cave mouths

allowed

f.g: let him go away safely

f.g: Hebrew shalom — wholeness, well-being.

baggage, supplies

roasted grain

f.w: any that pisseth against the wall
